'''Vladimir Petrovich Torchilin''' ({{langx|ru|Владимир Петрович Торчилин}}; born 1946) is a [[Soviet Union|Soviet]]-born [[United States|American]] [[biochemist]], [[pharmacologist]] and expert in medical [[nanotechnology]].<ref name="resu">{{cite web |title=Vladimir P. Torchilin Curriculum vitae |url=https://bouve.northeastern.edu/assets/uploads/sites/14/2014/07/CVtorchilin_2019.pdf |website=Center for Pharmaceutical Biotechnology and Nanomedicine |publisher=School of Pharmacy, Bouvé College of Health Sciences, Northeastern University |access-date=6 January 2022 |location=Boston |archive-date=6 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220106104147/https://bouve.northeastern.edu/assets/uploads/sites/14/2014/07/CVtorchilin_2019.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was University Distinguished Professor of Pharmaceutical Sciences and Director of the Center for Pharmaceutical Biotechnology and Nanomedicine at [[Northeastern University]] in Boston, where he served from 1998 to 2026, and has been Professor Emeritus since 2026.<ref name="bouve">{{cite web |author=Northeastern University, Bouvé College of Health Sciences |title=Vladimir Torchilin |website=Faculty directory |url=https://bouve.northeastern.edu/directory/vladimir-torchilin/}}</ref><ref name="cv2024">{{cite web |last=Torchilin |first=Vladimir P. |title=Curriculum Vitae |publisher=Northeastern University School of Pharmacy |date=2024 |url=https://bouve.northeastern.edu/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/CV-Torchilin-Vladimir-Northeastern-24.pdf}}</ref> Before joining Northeastern he was an associate professor of radiology at Harvard Medical School.<ref name="CRS">{{Cite web|title=Interview with a Luminary: Vladimir P. Torchilin, Ph.D., D.Sc.|url=https://www.controlledreleasesociety.org/interview-luminary-vladimir-p-torchilin-phd-dsc|website=Controlled Release Society}}</ref>

Torchilin has published more than 650 scientific papers and reviews, written and edited 15 books and holds more than 40 patents.<ref name="bouve" /> According to Google Scholar, his papers have received more than 105,000 citations, with an h-index of 142; these figures change over time.<ref name="scholar">{{cite web |title=Vladimir Torchilin |website=Google Scholar |type=Author profile |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=OKSa6s8AAAAJ&hl=en}}</ref>

In 2011 Times Higher Education ranked him second among the world's top scientists in pharmacology and toxicology for 2000–2010, a list based on publication counts and citation data.<ref name="the">{{cite web |author=Times Higher Education |title=Top scientists in pharmacology and toxicology |type=Thomson Reuters Essential Science Indicators data, 2000–2010 |url=https://www.timeshighereducation.com/node/76256}}</ref><ref name="nunews">{{cite news |author=Northeastern University |title=Torchilin among most-cited world scientists |work=Northeastern News |url=https://news.northeastern.edu/?p=11770}}</ref> In 2021 an Elsevier/Stanford analysis ranked him as the highest-cited of more than 130,000 researchers ranked in pharmacology and pharmacy.<ref name="bouve" /><ref name="topcited">{{Cite web|title=Bouvé College Distinguished Professor Recognized as Top-Cited Researcher in Category|url=https://bouve.northeastern.edu/2021/12/10/bouve-college-distinguished-professor-recognized-as-top-cited-researcher-in-category/|website=Northeastern University Bouve College of Health Sciences|date=10 December 2021|access-date=13 December 2021|archive-date=13 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211213031533/https://bouve.northeastern.edu/2021/12/10/bouve-college-distinguished-professor-recognized-as-top-cited-researcher-in-category/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was named a Clarivate Citation Laureate in 2023<ref name="clarivate">{{cite web |author=Clarivate |title=Clarivate Unveils Citation Laureates 2023 – Annual List of Researchers of Nobel Class |date=19 September 2023 |url=https://clarivate.com/news/clarivate-unveils-citation-laureates-2023-annual-list-of-researchers-of-nobel-class/}}</ref> and an inaugural Highly Ranked Scholar by ScholarGPS in 2024.<ref name="scholargps">{{cite web |author=ScholarGPS |title=Vladimir P. Torchilin |type=Scholar profile |url=https://scholargps.com/scholars/60733304247260/vladimir-p-torchilin}}</ref> He is also a writer and a member of the Union of Moscow Writers.<ref name="abebooks">{{cite web |author=AbeBooks |title=The Netsuke from San Francisco |type=author biography and publication details |url=https://www.abebooks.com/Netsuke-San-Francisco-Torchilin-Vladimir-Austin/31754607025/bd}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Torchilin was born in Moscow, then in the Soviet Union, in 1946.<ref name="abebooks" /> He received a [[Master of Science]] from [[Moscow State University]] in 1968, and his PhD in 1971 and DSc in 1981 from the same university.<ref name="cv2024" /><ref name="CRS" /> In the Soviet Union he worked at the Institute of Experimental Cardiology of the National Cardiology Research Center, on the polymeric modification of thrombolytic enzymes.<ref name="CRS" /> In 1982 he received the [[Lenin Prize]] of the USSR in science and technology.<ref name="CRS" /><ref name="resu" /><ref name="lenin">{{cite journal |title=The Lenin Prizes for 1982 |journal=The Current Digest of the Soviet Press |date=1982 |volume=34 |issue=16 |page=14 |publisher=American Association for the Advancement of Slavic Studies |location=University of Virginia}}</ref> He emigrated to the United States in 1990.<ref name="abebooks" /><ref name="nglobal">{{cite news |author=Northeastern Global News |title=Biochemist, author, art collector, Soviet émigré. How Vladimir Torchilin became a renowned scientist on both sides of the Iron Curtain |date=16 August 2023 |url=https://news.northeastern.edu/2023/08/16/magazine/vladimir-torchilin-biochemist/}}</ref>

==Career==
In 1991 Torchilin joined [[Massachusetts General Hospital]] and Harvard Medical School as head of the Chemistry Program at the Center for Imaging and Pharmaceutical Research and associate professor of radiology.<ref name="CRS" /> From 1998 he was at Northeastern University, where he chaired the Department of Pharmaceutical Sciences (1998–2008), was Distinguished Professor of Pharmaceutical Sciences (from 2012) and directed the Center for Pharmaceutical Biotechnology and Nanomedicine (from 2005).<ref name="cv2024" /><ref name="resu" /><ref name="JCR">{{Cite journal|title=Vladimir Torchilin Review Editor|url=https://www.journals.elsevier.com/journal-of-controlled-release/editorial-board/vladimir-torchilin|journal=Journal of Controlled Release|publisher=Elsevier|location=Boston}}</ref> He retired from the directorship and became Professor Emeritus in 2026.<ref name="bouve" />

Torchilin also led Northeastern's Center for Translational Cancer Nanomedicine, which was funded by a five-year, $13.5 million grant from the National Cancer Institute.<ref name="nunews" /> His work helped Northeastern become the first non-Ivy League university to receive a Center for Cancer Nanotechnology Excellence grant.<ref name="nglobal" />

==Research==
Torchilin's research concerns [[liposome]]s, lipid-core [[micelle]]s, biomedical polymers, drug delivery and targeting, pharmaceutical nanocarriers and experimental cancer therapy and immunology.<ref name="CRS" /><ref name="nglobal" /><ref name="JCR" /> His most-cited papers include a 2005 review of liposomes as pharmaceutical carriers in ''Nature Reviews Drug Discovery'' and later reviews of micellar and multifunctional nanocarriers.<ref name="scholar" />

==Editorial and professional service==
Torchilin is Editor-in-Chief of ''Current Drug Discovery Technologies''<ref name="bentham68">{{cite web |author=Bentham Science |title=Current Drug Discovery Technologies: Editorial Board |url=https://www.benthamscience.com/journal/68/editorial-board}}</ref> and Co-Editor-in-Chief of ''Current Pharmaceutical Biotechnology''.<ref name="bentham30">{{cite web |author=Bentham Science |title=Current Pharmaceutical Biotechnology: Editorial Board |url=https://benthamscience.com/journal/30/editorial-board}}</ref> He is also Editor of the Jenny Stanford Series on Biomedical Nanotechnology, Co-Editor of the Wiley series Advances in Pharmaceutical Technologies and Associate Editor of Biomedical Microdevices.<ref name="bio">Torchilin, Vladimir P. Short biography and lists of awards and books, supplied by the subject; unpublished.</ref> He serves on the editorial boards of Bioconjugate Chemistry, Advanced Drug Delivery Reviews and other journals in drug delivery, nanomedicine and pharmaceutical sciences.<ref name="bouve" /> He was Editor-in-Chief of ''Drug Delivery'' from 2003 to 2023 and Review Editor of the ''Journal of Controlled Release'' from 2010 to 2023.<ref name="bio" /><ref name="JCR" /> He was President of the Controlled Release Society in 2005–2006,<ref name="hstalks">{{cite web |author=HSTalks |title=Prof. Vladimir P. Torchilin |url=https://hstalks.com/expert/618/prof-vladimir-p-torchilin}}</ref> and has mentored more than 50 PhD students.<ref name="bio" />

==Literary work and collecting==
Torchilin is a member of the Union of Moscow Writers.<ref name="abebooks" /> His short stories have been published in literary magazines in the USSR since the early 1980s and, after 1990, in Russian-language literary magazines in Russia and the United States.<ref name="bio" /><ref name="livelib">{{Cite web|url=http://www.livelib.ru/author/247026|title = Владимир Торчилин}}</ref> He is the author of nine books of short stories in Russian, published in Russia and the United States, and of a book of verse published in Germany in 2026. His first book in English, ''The Netsuke from San Francisco'', was published by Austin Macauley Publishers in 2024.<ref name="bio" /><ref name="hoopla">{{cite web |author=Hoopla / library catalogue |title=The Netsuke From San Francisco |publisher=Austin Macauley Publishers |date=2024 |url=https://discover.aclib.us/Hoopla/16554074}}</ref> He is also an art and book collector, and paintings from his collections have been shown at multiple exhibitions.<ref name="nglobal" /><ref name="bio" />

==Personal life==
Torchilin lives in Boston with his wife, Vera. They have one daughter and three grandchildren.<ref name="bio" />
